A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same position paper. Their main text, four corresponding figures, references, and appendices support reliable comparison despite changes in scope and organization.

before.justification: v1 synthesizes existing literature and proposes research directions. Described experiments and simulations belong to cited studies; Appendices A–B contain a literature map and historical roadmap.

after.justification: v2 remains a literature-based position paper. Its expanded literature map, limitations, and future directions introduce no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Both retain the same three-role framework—data enhancers, task predictors, and agents—and the same five agent abilities. No proposed algorithm, architecture, training objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. The reframing from foreign language education to English education changes the stated scope, without changing empirically tested coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version performs baseline comparisons. Additional methods in v2’s Figure 4 are entries in a literature map, not experimentally evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version implements an experimental evaluation protocol. Appendix B’s recommendations for pedagogical evaluation and educational standards describe future work rather than adopted experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports its own ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. Section 5.3’s Error Analysis remains a description of a tutoring application, not a performed analysis.

E5.justification: Run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, and statistical uncertainty estimates are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No concrete experimental result entries, performance values, rankings, or study-specific qualitative outcomes are introduced or revised. The expanded literature map supplies citations rather than additional results.

T1.justification: Neither version contains formal mathematical assumptions, propositions, derivations, or proofs. The retained educational taxonomies and conceptual classifications do not introduce new formal theory.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the central claim from foreign language education generally to English education. This substantially changes its stated applicability, while retaining the three roles and the claim that LLMs should complement human tutors.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning infrastructure, socioeconomic barriers, learner populations, and human–LLM pedagogical interactions. New Appendix B specifies pedagogical evaluation, CEFR/CCSS alignment, and teacher oversight priorities beyond v1’s general recommendations. Conversely, v1 Section 6.1’s specific discussion of unvalidated memory-module learning benefits is removed.

D1.justification: No implementation settings, training recipe, hardware/runtime information, or code/data release instructions are added. The new links to educational standards support recommendations rather than reproducibility of an implemented study.

R1.justification: v2 adds literature including RECIPE, eRevise+RF, recent tutor-evaluation studies, and work on standards alignment and teacher collaboration. Schwind (1990) and Shetye (2024) are removed. These update the supporting literature while preserving the existing three-role taxonomy.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: v1 Appendix B’s roadmap enters Section 3, and Section 8’s Alternative Views moves to v2 Appendix C. v2 adds Limitations and a new Future Directions appendix, removes the separate Impact Statement, and changes domain terminology throughout.

P2.justification: The paper is reformatted from Letter to A4 with larger body text, wider margins, redesigned author/affiliation placement, and removed running headers. All four figures remain, but Figures 3 and 4 relocate, captions change, and Figure 4 is expanded and reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 extends v1’s general risk discussion with clearer practical limitations and more actionable priorities for pedagogical evaluation, educational standards, and teacher oversight. These modestly strengthen the position paper. Benefits are partly offset by losing the specific memory-evaluation caveat and by scope and editorial inconsistencies, including the erroneous 'Appendix 7' reference in Limitations.
